### DES-7: Legacy Cleanup And Migration Reporting

The current legacy cleanup path does not use hashes: it removes hardcoded candidate files and skill directories unconditionally. That heuristic cannot satisfy the requirement that only unmodified files are removed, so it is not ported verbatim.

The comparison basis is the instruction body, not the whole file, and it is compared against the canonical body **as it stood before this change**. A legacy artifact was generated by applying the previous release's per-platform transformation to the canonical artifact of that time, so its frontmatter was rewritten and, in one profile, its body was rewritten too. Comparing against the current canonical body would be wrong for two reasons: the transformation alone changes the bytes, and this change itself rewrites the guidance content, so the current body is not the baseline the legacy artifact was generated from. The implementation therefore keeps a snapshot of the pre-change canonical bodies and applies the declared legacy derivation to that snapshot; a legacy file that differs from the derived result is preserved and reported.

The legacy MiniMax global install is the concrete case. Its two extra skill directories sit inside the `skills/` directory of the user artifact root, and the same two directories are what the skills-only profile emits today, so for as long as that profile is active an install manifest claims them and they are not reported. They become reportable exactly when they stop being claimed, which is the correct signal.

The canonical set is the fourteen shipped skills plus the agent and the commands. A skills-only platform receives the agent and the commands as derived skills inside the artifact root, recorded as that platform's platform-side artifacts, so those paths are claimed by a manifest and are never mistaken for leftovers.

The backup option follows the same ownership rule. It copies the recorded artifact paths of the selected platform and scope, not the artifact root as a whole, because the artifact root is shared and a whole-root copy would sweep in unrelated user content.

Two exclusions matter. The rule that decides whether a leftover is reported is claim-based rather than location-based: a path is reported as a legacy candidate only when no current install manifest claims it. That is the only rule that works for the case that motivated it, because the legacy MiniMax directories live inside the `skills/` directory of the user artifact root and are also the current output of the skills-only profile for three platforms. A location-based rule would either hide them forever or report them while they are in use; a claim-based rule reports a genuine leftover and stays quiet about anything an active installation owns. And the legacy global cleanup path that treats `~/.agents` as a platform directory is retired, because that directory is now the canonical root itself and deleting from it would delete the current installation.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Detect["scan legacy platform roots"] --> Claim{"claimed by a current manifest?"}
    Claim -->|"yes"| Keep["leave untouched"]
    Claim -->|"no"| Compare{"body matches the pre-change baseline?"}
    Compare -->|"yes"| Remove["remove"]
    Compare -->|"no"| Report["report as candidate, preserve"]
    Report --> Migrate["migration candidate report"]
```

### DES-13: Distribution Channels And Installer Trust Boundary

The npm channel keeps the package name and remains an installation channel, but its shape changes: it no longer ships a Node entrypoint. Platform-specific packages are published alongside the main package and declared as optional dependencies, each carrying the release binary for one platform and architecture. The registry resolves the matching package, and the installer copies the binary out of it, verifies it against the digest published with that package, and performs no network access of its own.

This resolves what an earlier draft of the plan could not: obtaining a binary requires either the registry or a direct download, and a "thin installer that downloads the binary" cannot simultaneously claim to perform no network access. Making the registry the transport keeps the npm path free of a bespoke downloader, keeps npm's own integrity check in the chain, and keeps the provenance attestation meaningful for every package in it. The release pipeline cross-checks the digest published with each platform package against the checksum published with the GitHub Release.

Each platform package declares the operating system and the architecture it applies to, using npm's own vocabulary — `linux`, `darwin`, and `win32` with `x64` and `arm64` — so that the registry resolves exactly one package for the user. The release pipeline maps the Go build targets onto that vocabulary explicitly rather than assuming the two naming schemes agree.

The digest check performed by the installer is a corruption check, not a provenance check: the digest travels inside the package it authenticates. The provenance controls are the publisher's attestation and the release-time cross-check against the GitHub Release checksum.

When install scripts are disabled, the installer never executes and therefore cannot print anything. The package documentation states the binary location inside the resolved platform package and the manual command that links it, which is the only actor that can act in that state.

GitHub Releases carry the binaries and their checksums, and the Homebrew formula references a published release asset. Both external destinations — the Homebrew tap and the distribution repository — are created once and updated by the release pipeline.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Version["declared version"] --> Build["cross compile"]
    Build --> Release["GitHub Release assets and checksums"]
    Build --> PlatformPkgs["npm platform packages with digests"]
    PlatformPkgs --> Root["npm main package with optional dependencies"]
    Root --> Install["installer copies and verifies, no network"]
    Release --> Formula["Homebrew formula"]
    Release --> Distribution["distribution repository tree"]
```

### DES-15: Internal State Resolution

Not everything the CLI owns is an artifact. Three stores hold internal state, and each is resolved by rules the current implementation already applies, with environment overrides that users depend on:

| State | Location | Resolution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Install manifests | The configuration directory | `SDS_CONFIG_DIR`, else APPDATA on Windows, else XDG_CONFIG_HOME, else `~/.config/spec-driven-steroids` |

The configuration directory and the cache directory resolve by different rules, and collapsing them into one would silently relocate either store. The design keeps each resolution intact, including the fact that `SDS_CONFIG_DIR` names the store directory directly rather than a parent of it.

## Data Models

The descriptor is the primary data structure and must express every platform behavior the current implementation encodes in code.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class PlatformDescriptor {
        +string id
        +string displayName
        +string[] scopes
        +string scopeFallback
        +ArtifactRule[] artifacts
        +PathVariant[] pathVariants
        +SkipRule[] skipRules
        +CollisionRule[] collisionRules
        +PostInjectAction[] postInjectActions
        +string[] legacyRoots
        +string legacyProjectRoot
        +LegacyDerivation[] legacyDerivations
    }
    class ArtifactRule {
        +string kind
        +string source
        +string target
        +string mode
        +string filename
        +string serialization
        +FrontmatterSpec frontmatter
    }
    class PathVariant {
        +string operatingSystem
        +string environmentVariable
        +string base
        +string[] segments
    }
    class PostInjectAction {
        +string kind
        +string scope
        +string targetFile
        +map parameters
    }
    class FrontmatterSpec {
        +map fields
        +map additionalFields
        +map kindOverrides
    }
    class InstallManifest {
        +number version
        +string kind
        +string scope
        +string projectRoot
        +string platform
        +InstalledFile[] files
    }
    class InstalledFile {
        +string path
        +string sha256
        +string[] claimingPlatforms
    }
    class LegacyDerivation {
        +string platform
        +string kind
        +string scope
        +string transformation
    }
```

`InstallManifest.kind` distinguishes the canonical manifest from a platform manifest, which is the additive field that keeps the version 1 format readable by both implementations.

## Error Handling

| Error Condition | Response | Recovery |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Descriptor missing a required field | Reject the descriptor, report the named field | Correct the descriptor; no platform writes occur |
| Requested scope unsupported by a platform | Apply the descriptor's declared fallback scope | Inject at the fallback scope; the effective scope is reported |
| Remote bundle fails digest or limit checks | Fall back to the embedded bundle, report the reason | User may force the bundled source explicitly |
| Remote bundle lacks the required skill contract | Fall back to the embedded bundle, report the reason | Same as above |
| Installed file digest differs from the manifest | Preserve the file and report it | User resolves manually or forces cleanup |
| Legacy file content differs from the canonical artifact | Preserve the file and report it as a migration candidate | User resolves manually |
| Packaged layout violates a marketplace schema | Fail the packaging run and report the violation | Fix the packer; nothing is published |
| Emitted tree contains a symbolic link or a native binary | Fail the packaging run | Fix the packer |
| Platform package digest does not match the binary | Refuse to place the binary | Reinstall from a verified release |
| Install scripts disabled | The published package documentation names the binary location inside the resolved platform package and the manual command that links it | Link the binary manually |
| Release tag does not match the declared version | Fail the release before any publish | Nothing published |

### Breaking Changes

| Change | Description | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Installed file locations | Managed files move from platform directories to the artifact root, with platform-side artifacts beside them | The artifact root is written for every scope and the doctor command reports the resolved set and layer |
| Install manifest addressing | Manifests split into canonical and platform kinds and the lookup key changes | The resolver probes the legacy key derived from the platform root, so existing installations are found and cleaned |
| npm package payload | The package no longer contains the CLI implementation | The installer places the release binary from the resolved platform package; the package version still matches the release |
| Minimum runtime | Node.js is no longer required | Node.js users gain; no user loses a capability |
| Legacy cleanup behavior | A legacy file whose body differs from the canonical body is now preserved instead of removed | The file is reported so the user can decide |
| Backup scope | The backup option now copies only the recorded artifact paths instead of the whole platform root | The previous behavior copied the root, which under the new layout would sweep in unrelated user content |
| Install manifest addressing | Manifests are keyed by project root and split into canonical and platform kinds | The resolver probes the exact legacy filenames, so existing installations are still found |
| Emptied directories | Cleanup stops at the directory that owns a removed file, so a shared skill directory is left in place instead of being removed | The directory is left empty rather than deleted; the previous behavior removed it |
| Validation diagnostics | Diagnostic text is now produced by a different runtime | Golden fixtures captured from the current release enforce identical output |

| Test Type | Coverage Goal | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unit | Descriptor validation, path variants, serialization profiles, manifest hashing, EARS grammar | Port the existing unit assertions rather than restating them |
| Integration | Injection per platform, artifact root layout, platform-side emission, cleanup with modified files, legacy reporting | Each emission mode exercised end to end |
| Parity | The existing suite re-expressed against the Go CLI, compared to the golden fixtures | Verdict, message, exit code and file effects compared to the recorded behavior |

| E2E | Install through the npm channel, run the version command, inject into a temporary project | Smoke-test the distributed artifact, not only the source tree |

### Rollback Plan

| Scenario | Rollback Steps | Time to Recovery |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Go CLI released with a behavior regression | Revert the release tag, republish the previous binary through the same pipeline, repoint the Homebrew formula | Under 15 minutes |
| Users need the previous installation layout | Republish the TypeScript CLI as the npm package and restore the previous release assets | Under 30 minutes |
| A platform-side artifact proves unreadable by its platform | Ship a descriptor correction that changes the emission mode for that platform | Under 15 minutes |
| Marketplace publication causes an incident | Withdraw the catalog entry from the distribution repository; installed packages continue to work from their local copy | Under 15 minutes |
| Legacy cleanup misidentifies a user file | Restore from the reported path; the ownership rule already prevents removal of any path the manifest does not claim | Immediate |

# Requirements

## Overview

Spec-Driven Steroids ships a CLI that injects a spec-driven workflow into AI coding tools. Two structural costs limit how far the product can grow.

The first cost is the runtime. The published package is a Node.js program with five runtime dependencies, so every user provisions a Node.js runtime and a package manager to install what is, functionally, a static bundle of prompts and a handful of filesystem commands.

The second cost is platform adaptation. Supporting a new AI coding tool currently requires writing code, not configuration: a scope resolver per platform, a format and frontmatter configuration per platform, and a transformation pipeline that rewrites canonical content differently for each target. Platform identity, content transformation, and injection orchestration are interleaved, which makes each new platform a change to runtime behavior rather than an addition to a registry.

This change re-architects the product around two commitments. First, the CLI becomes a first-class native Go binary with no runtime dependency, preserving the full command surface, exit codes, and output contracts that CI pipelines and users already depend on. Second, every SDS-managed artifact lives under a single platform-neutral artifact root — `.agents/` at project scope, `~/.agents/` at user scope — and platform differences are expressed as declarative descriptor data, so that adding a platform becomes a configuration change and canonical content is never rewritten per target.

The artifact root is not a new convention: the current release already writes MiniMax Code global skills to `~/.agents/skills`, Antigravity project scope to `.agents`, and Codex reads its native marketplace catalog from `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`. This change generalizes that location into the product's single artifact root. The root is a *shared* directory in some hosts, so the CLI owns only the paths it records and never removes content it did not create.

The change also consolidates the repository guidance artifacts: the contribution workflow and the code style conventions currently split across `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `STYLEGUIDE.md` become a single `CONVENTIONS.md`.

The distribution model changes with the runtime. GitHub Releases and Homebrew become the primary channels, while npm continues to serve as an installation channel that places the release binary for the user's platform. In parallel, the shipped artifacts gain a distribution form the AI tooling ecosystem already understands: a portable Agent Plugin package, plus the marketplace catalogs that let users install it from Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, MiniMax Code, and Gemini CLI without running the CLI at all.

Lane rationale: full. This change replaces the runtime of a published CLI, alters the on-disk layout that every existing installation depends on, rewrites the release path, and adds a publication surface to third-party marketplaces. Separate requirements, design, and tasks reviews resolve materially different uncertainties in the runtime migration, the artifact-root model, the packaging format, and the compatibility strategy.

## Glossary

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| Artifact root | The `.agents/` directory that holds every SDS-managed artifact, at project scope inside the repository or at user scope under the home directory. |
| Canonical artifact | A file whose content does not depend on the target platform and which SDS never rewrites to suit a platform. |
| Platform descriptor | Declarative metadata describing where a platform reads artifacts, how it names them, which frontmatter fields it requires, and how each artifact kind reaches it. |
| Platform-side artifact | A file written outside the artifact root because a platform reads its own directory instead of the artifact root. |
| Internal state | Install manifests and the template cache, which are SDS bookkeeping rather than injected artifacts and live in the platform configuration directory. |
| Portable Agent Plugin | A distribution package whose root holds a `plugin.json` manifest, a `skills/` directory, and an optional `mcp.json`, consumable as-is by several AI coding tools. |
| Marketplace catalog | The JSON document a platform reads to discover installable packages, listing each package name and where to fetch it. |
| Distribution channel | A mechanism that delivers the product to a user: GitHub Releases, Homebrew, the npm registry, or a platform marketplace. |
| Guidance set | The repository-level documents that the shipped guidance instructions direct the host to produce: `AGENTS.md`, `CONVENTIONS.md`, `TESTING.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, and `SECURITY.md`. |
| Legacy install | Files written into platform-specific directories by a CLI release published before this change, recorded in a version 1 install manifest or detectable by content match. |
| Rule graph | The local store of architectural decisions and workflow rules, held as JSON files with lifecycle state, provenance, and version history. |

## Assumptions

- Node.js is not required to run the published CLI after this change, and no runtime package dependency remains in the distributed artifact.
- The Go toolchain and the release runners can cross-compile binaries for the supported operating system and architecture matrix.
- The remote template bundle and manifest schema stay backward compatible, so template bundles published before this change remain resolvable, and the required-skill contract remains the fourteen skill directories listed by the current registry.
- The version 1 install manifest format stays readable, so installations created by earlier releases can still be cleaned up and migrated.
- The npm package remains a public installation channel that places the release binary for the user's platform and architecture through platform-specific packages resolved by the registry.
- A Homebrew tap and a marketplace distribution repository exist outside this repository and are updated by the release pipeline.
- Marketplace vendors that require a vendor account, a submission form, or a human review keep that publication step manual.
- Marketplace listings that require open source are satisfied by the existing public repository.
- The landing page, the content of the individual workflow skills, and the hosting of the remote template bundle are outside the scope of this change.
- Users who already customized `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `STYLEGUIDE.md` keep access to their content during the consolidation into `CONVENTIONS.md`.

## Requirements

### REQ-1: Dependency-Free Native CLI And Distribution Channels

**User Story:** As a user of the CLI, I want to install a single native executable from a channel I already trust, so that I can use Spec-Driven Steroids without provisioning a Node.js runtime.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1.1 THE `sds` CLI SHALL execute as a compiled native binary that requires no Node.js runtime and no runtime package dependency.

1.2 THE `sds` CLI SHALL expose the commands of the current release — inject, clean, doctor, repair, uninstall, templates, validate and stewardship — together with the version flag and the help output, with unchanged argument names and exit codes, and with machine-readable payloads extended only by additive fields.

1.3 THE `sds` CLI SHALL remain installable from the npm registry under the package name `spec-driven-steroids`.

1.4 THE release pipeline SHALL publish a standalone binary as a GitHub Release asset for each of the supported operating system and architecture pairs, which are Linux, macOS and Windows on the x64 and arm64 architectures.

1.5 THE `sds` CLI SHALL be installable through a maintained Homebrew formula that references a published GitHub Release.

1.6 WHEN a user installs the npm package, THEN the npm installer SHALL copy the binary shipped in the platform package that the registry resolved for the user's operating system and architecture, verifying that binary against the digest published with that platform package and performing no network access of its own, with every platform package declaring the operating system and architecture it applies to so that the registry resolves exactly one of them.

1.7 WHEN a release is published, THEN the release pipeline SHALL publish the platform binaries before the corresponding npm package version is published.

1.8 THE `sds --version` command SHALL report the release version shared by the binary, the npm package, and the Homebrew formula.

1.9 THE `sds` CLI SHALL expose a packaging command that emits the portable distribution artifacts without contacting any marketplace.

### REQ-2: Platform-Neutral Artifact Root

**User Story:** As a user, I want every SDS-managed artifact to live in one predictable directory, so that I understand what the CLI writes and can reason about the result without platform-specific knowledge.

#### Acceptance Criteria

2.1 THE `sds` CLI SHALL write every canonical artifact under the project artifact root `.agents/` when the project scope is selected, and under the user artifact root `~/.agents/` when the user scope is selected, keeping the install manifest store in the configuration directory, the template bundle cache in the cache directory, and the rule graph under the user artifact root instead.

2.2 THE `sds` CLI SHALL use the same internal layout for skills, agents, and commands in the project artifact root and in the user artifact root.

2.3 THE `sds` CLI SHALL define the artifact root layout as a skills directory holding one directory per skill with its `SKILL.md` and references, an agents directory, and a commands directory, with the user artifact root additionally holding the stewardship subtree.

2.4 WHEN a project artifact and a user artifact share a name, THEN the `sds` CLI SHALL resolve the project artifact in preference to the user artifact, reporting the resolved artifact set with the layer that supplied each artifact.

2.5 THE `sds` CLI SHALL NOT create a platform-specific directory outside the artifact root unless the user selects that platform for injection, with the descriptor of that platform declaring whether the platform reads the artifact root directly or receives a platform-side artifact, and with the ownership of that directory recorded so that cleanup never removes it.

2.6 THE `sds` CLI SHALL report the resolved artifact root, the written artifact paths, and the effective scope in the machine-readable output of the inject command.

2.7 THE `sds` CLI SHALL own only the artifact paths it records in its install manifest, leaving every other content of the artifact root or of a platform directory untouched.

### REQ-3: Declarative Platform Descriptors Instead Of Code-Level Adaptation

**User Story:** As a maintainer, I want supporting a new AI coding tool to be a configuration change, so that the product can grow without growing a transformation pipeline.

#### Acceptance Criteria

3.1 THE `sds` CLI SHALL express each platform's artifact locations, per-operating-system and per-environment path variants, file naming, frontmatter composition rules, per-artifact-kind overrides, scope support, scope fallback, target-collision rules, legacy derivation rules, and post-injection actions as declarative descriptor data.

3.2 THE `sds` CLI SHALL emit the canonical artifact body unmodified for every platform whose descriptor declares the canonical format.

3.3 WHEN a platform descriptor declares a derived serialization, THEN the `sds` CLI SHALL derive the platform-side artifact from the canonical body using the transformation declared by that descriptor, with the descriptor stating the substitutions that serialization applies to the body.

3.4 WHEN a platform does not read the artifact root directly, THEN the `sds` CLI SHALL write a platform-side artifact containing the canonical body as the declared serialization transforms it, together with the frontmatter composed by the descriptor, without using symbolic links or pointer files for that purpose.

3.5 THE `sds` CLI SHALL record every written path and every platform-side path in the install manifest, with a content digest for each recorded file and with the producing platform recorded for each platform-side path.

3.6 WHEN a platform is added to the supported set, THEN the `sds` CLI SHALL require no change to the canonical artifact templates and no change to the injection orchestration code.

3.7 THE `sds` CLI SHALL reject a platform descriptor that omits the platform identifier, the display name, at least one supported scope, at least one artifact rule, or the required fields of that rule, reporting which field is missing.

3.8 THE `sds` CLI SHALL treat a requested scope that a platform does not support as the platform's declared fallback scope.

3.9 THE `sds` CLI SHALL resolve every path and state directory using the same environment variable precedence as the current release, including `APPDATA`, `USERPROFILE`, `LOCALAPPDATA`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, `SDS_CONFIG_DIR`, `SDS_TEMPLATE_CACHE_DIR`, and `SDS_HOME`.

### REQ-4: Compatibility With Existing Installations

**User Story:** As an existing user, I want my current installation recognized and migratable, so that moving to the rewritten CLI does not orphan files or discard my customizations.

#### Acceptance Criteria

4.1 WHEN the `sds` CLI looks for an install manifest, THEN the `sds` CLI SHALL read the manifest written by a previous release at the legacy filename key, which is `<platform>-global-global.json` for the user scope and `<platform>-project-<twelve hexadecimal characters of the pre-change platform root>` for the project scope, as well as at the current filename key, with the pre-change platform root of every supported platform declared as descriptor data.

4.2 WHEN the user requests cleanup of a legacy install, THEN the `sds` CLI SHALL remove a previously installed file only when its instruction body still matches the canonical body it was generated from, compared against the canonical body as it stood before this change and after applying the legacy per-platform derivation recorded for that platform, preserving and reporting every file whose body differs.

4.3 IF a legacy installed file was modified by the user, THEN the `sds` CLI SHALL preserve the modified file and report it instead of deleting or overwriting it.

4.4 WHEN the `sds` CLI injects into a project that contains artifacts written under a legacy platform directory other than the artifact root, THEN the `sds` CLI SHALL report as migration candidates those of those files that no current install manifest claims.

4.5 THE `sds` CLI SHALL read and write the version 1 install manifest format, including the recorded SHA-256 digest of each installed file, adding any new information as an additive field so that a manifest written by either implementation parses in the other.

4.6 THE `sds` CLI SHALL expose a dry-run mode for every command that writes to or removes files.

4.7 WHEN the `sds` CLI removes an empty parent directory after cleanup, THEN the `sds` CLI SHALL stop at the directory that owns the removed file, leaving that emptied owning directory in place and never removing a directory the install manifest does not claim.

4.8 THE `sds` CLI SHALL record the canonical artifacts of the artifact root separately from the platform-side artifacts of each platform, reconciling the claims of every manifest before removing a path so that removing one platform's installation never removes an artifact another platform still claims.

4.9 WHEN the backup option is used, THEN the `sds` CLI SHALL copy only the recorded artifact paths of the selected platform and scope without copying the whole artifact root.

### REQ-5: Consolidated Guidance Artifacts

**User Story:** As a user, I want one conventions document instead of separate contribution and style guides, so that my repository guidance is shorter to read and easier to maintain.

#### Acceptance Criteria

5.1 THE shipped guidance instructions SHALL direct the host to produce the guidance set consisting of `AGENTS.md`, `CONVENTIONS.md`, `TESTING.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, and `SECURITY.md`.

5.2 THE shipped guidance instructions SHALL direct the host to stop producing `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `STYLEGUIDE.md` as separate artifacts.

5.3 WHEN the guidance instructions are applied to a repository that holds `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `STYLEGUIDE.md`, THEN the host SHALL merge the existing contribution workflow and code style content into `CONVENTIONS.md` under section headings that preserve the original wording of user-authored rules.

5.4 WHEN the doctor command runs in a repository that holds `CONVENTIONS.md`, THEN the `sds` CLI SHALL report any `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `STYLEGUIDE.md` it also holds as superseded.

5.5 THE shipped guidance instructions SHALL direct the host to leave a guidance file that requires no change unwritten.

5.6 THE shipped guidance instructions SHALL direct the host to preserve user-authored rules when consolidating the contribution and style content, stating the merge rule that the guidance contract test asserts.

5.7 THE shipped guidance references SHALL discover `CONVENTIONS.md` in place of `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `STYLEGUIDE.md`.

5.8 WHEN this change ships, THEN the repository's own root guidance documents `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `STYLEGUIDE.md` SHALL be replaced by a single root `CONVENTIONS.md`.

### REQ-6: Behavioral Parity Of Validation And Stewardship

**User Story:** As a user, I want validators and stored rules to behave exactly as they do today, so that my CI gates and my accumulated knowledge keep working after the rewrite.

#### Acceptance Criteria

6.1 THE `sds` CLI SHALL produce the same validation verdict, error code, and diagnostic message for the same invalid input as the current release.

6.2 THE `sds` CLI SHALL classify EARS criteria, requirement identifiers, spec structure, and traceability exactly as the current release classifies them.

6.3 THE `sds` CLI SHALL read and write rule graph files in the existing on-disk format, so that rules stored before the rewrite remain retrievable.

6.4 WHEN the `sds` CLI stores a rule, THEN the `sds` CLI SHALL preserve the existing write lock and atomic-rename guarantees for the rule store.

6.5 THE `sds` CLI SHALL retain the exit code contract of the current release, where a successful validation exits with 0, a validation or partial failure exits with 1, and a usage error exits with 2.

6.6 THE `sds` CLI SHALL preserve the project-scoped rule resolution behavior in which a project rule takes precedence and retrieval falls back to global rules.

### REQ-7: Remote Template Bundle Continuity

**User Story:** As a user, I want the template bundles published before this change to keep working, so that the rewrite does not strand my installations.

#### Acceptance Criteria

7.1 THE `sds` CLI SHALL resolve a remote template bundle published with the current manifest and bundle schema, requiring the same fourteen skill directories that the current registry requires.

7.2 IF a remote bundle lacks a required skill contract, THEN the `sds` CLI SHALL fall back to the bundled templates and report the reason for the fallback.

7.3 WHEN the published manifest supplies a digest, THEN the `sds` CLI SHALL verify the bundle against that digest before use.

7.4 THE `sds` CLI SHALL reject a template bundle whose declared minimum CLI version is higher than the running binary version.

7.5 THE `sds` CLI SHALL embed the canonical artifacts in the binary, so that injection succeeds with no network access.

7.6 THE `sds` CLI SHALL preserve the containment, file-count, and size limits applied to a remote bundle before extraction.

### REQ-8: Release And Version Consistency

**User Story:** As a maintainer, I want one version source of truth, so that no channel disagrees about a release.

#### Acceptance Criteria

8.1 THE release process SHALL derive the binary version, the npm package version, the Homebrew formula reference, the template bundle version, and the marketplace package version from a single declared version in the repository.

8.2 WHEN a release is published, THEN the release pipeline SHALL publish the platform binaries, the npm packages, the Homebrew formula, the template bundle, and the marketplace package for the same version.

8.3 WHEN a release tag does not match the declared repository version, THEN the release pipeline SHALL fail before publishing any artifact.

8.4 THE release pipeline SHALL run the test suite and the packaged-artifact smoke check before publishing any artifact.

8.5 THE release pipeline SHALL publish the npm packages with the provenance attestation that the current release configuration requests.

8.6 THE release process SHALL update the Homebrew formula reference and the marketplace package version in the same release that publishes the binary.

### REQ-9: Portable Agent Plugin Packaging

**User Story:** As a user of an AI coding tool, I want to install the Spec-Driven workflow the way I install any other extension, so that I can adopt it without running the CLI at all.

#### Acceptance Criteria

9.1 THE `sds` CLI SHALL emit a portable Agent Plugin package whose root holds a `plugin.json` manifest, a `skills/` directory, and an optional `mcp.json`.

9.2 THE `sds` CLI SHALL generate the portable package from the canonical artifacts without altering the canonical artifact content.

9.3 WHEN the `sds` CLI emits a portable package, THEN the `sds` CLI SHALL reference every packaged skill in the `plugin.json` manifest.

9.4 WHEN a supported marketplace requires a vendor-specific manifest, THEN the `sds` CLI SHALL emit that manifest beside the portable manifest without altering the portable manifest, except for the Gemini CLI extension manifest, which belongs at the root of the distribution tree instead.

9.5 THE `sds` CLI SHALL validate the emitted package against the documented layout of every marketplace that consumes it, reporting each violation and rejecting an emitted tree that contains a symbolic link or a native binary.

9.6 THE `sds` CLI SHALL produce the portable package as a directory tree that a git repository can publish directly.

### REQ-10: Marketplace Catalogs And Publication

**User Story:** As a maintainer, I want one artifact set that the major tool marketplaces can consume, so that publishing to each of them is a push rather than a rebuild.

#### Acceptance Criteria

10.1 THE `sds` CLI SHALL emit the marketplace catalog, the root manifest, or the package subtree for every supported marketplace at the path that marketplace reads, reporting a registration step that is not a file as manual.

10.2 WHEN the `sds` CLI emits more than one marketplace catalog, THEN the `sds` CLI SHALL make every catalog reference the same canonical package directory and the same package version.

10.3 THE `sds` CLI SHALL emit each catalog so that a user can install the package from that marketplace without editing the catalog by hand.

10.4 THE `sds` CLI SHALL produce the package and catalog artifacts in a form that can be published by pushing them to a git repository, with the release pipeline generating that distribution tree outside this repository's working tree before pushing it to the distribution repository.

10.5 WHEN a marketplace requires a vendor account, a submission form, or a human review, THEN the `sds` CLI SHALL record that publication step as manual instead of attempting to automate it.

10.6 THE `sds` CLI SHALL report for each supported marketplace whether its publication step is automated or manual.

10.7 THE `sds` CLI SHALL keep the marketplace package version equal to the version declared for the release.

### REQ-11: Installer Trust Boundary

**User Story:** As a user installing from npm, I want the binary I receive to be verifiable, so that installing the CLI does not widen my trust surface.

#### Acceptance Criteria

11.1 THE npm installer SHALL obtain the binary only from the platform package that the registry resolved, never downloading it from another location.

11.2 THE npm installer SHALL verify the binary against the digest published with the platform package before placing it as a corruption check, refusing to place a binary whose digest does not match, while the publisher's attestation and the release-time checksum cross-check remain the provenance controls.

11.3 WHEN install scripts are disabled, THEN the published package documentation SHALL name the binary location inside the resolved platform package and the manual command that links it.

11.4 THE release pipeline SHALL cross-check the digest published with each platform package against the checksum published with the GitHub Release, publishing the platform packages before the main package that depends on them.

### REQ-12: Artifact Root Ownership

**User Story:** As a user who keeps my own agent skills in the shared agent directory, I want the CLI to touch only its own files, so that enabling it never removes or rewrites my work.

#### Acceptance Criteria

12.1 THE `sds` CLI SHALL remove only the artifact paths recorded in an install manifest, never removing a directory it did not create.

12.2 WHEN the artifact root contains an entry that no install manifest claims, THEN the `sds` CLI SHALL preserve that entry, including unrelated skill directories, treating such a directory as shared with other agents.

12.3 WHEN cleanup removes an empty parent directory, THEN the `sds` CLI SHALL stop at the directory that owns the removed file without continuing upward.

12.4 THE `sds` CLI SHALL report a legacy artifact as a migration candidate only when no current install manifest claims that path, never reporting a canonical artifact or a path claimed by a current manifest as a legacy candidate.

#!/bin/sh
#
# An example hook script to block unannotated tags from entering.
# Called by "git receive-pack" with arguments: refname sha1-old sha1-new
#
# To enable this hook, rename this file to "update".
#
# Config
# ------
# hooks.allowunannotated
#   This boolean sets whether unannotated tags will be allowed into the
#   repository.  By default they won't be.
# hooks.allowdeletetag
#   This boolean sets whether deleting tags will be allowed in the
#   repository.  By default they won't be.
# hooks.allowmodifytag
#   This boolean sets whether a tag may be modified after creation. By default
#   it won't be.
# hooks.allowdeletebranch
#   This boolean sets whether deleting branches will be allowed in the
#   repository.  By default they won't be.
# hooks.denycreatebranch
#   This boolean sets whether remotely creating branches will be denied
#   in the repository.  By default this is allowed.
#

# --- Command line
refname="$1"
oldrev="$2"
newrev="$3"

# --- Safety check
if [ -z "$GIT_DIR" ]; then
	echo "Don't run this script from the command line." >&2
	echo " (if you want, you could supply GIT_DIR then run" >&2
	echo "  $0 <ref> <oldrev> <newrev>)" >&2
	exit 1
fi

if [ -z "$refname" -o -z "$oldrev" -o -z "$newrev" ]; then
	echo "usage: $0 <ref> <oldrev> <newrev>" >&2
	exit 1
fi

# --- Config
allowunannotated=$(git config --type=bool hooks.allowunannotated)
allowdeletebranch=$(git config --type=bool hooks.allowdeletebranch)
denycreatebranch=$(git config --type=bool hooks.denycreatebranch)
allowdeletetag=$(git config --type=bool hooks.allowdeletetag)
allowmodifytag=$(git config --type=bool hooks.allowmodifytag)

# check for no description
projectdesc=$(sed -e '1q' "$GIT_DIR/description")
case "$projectdesc" in
"Unnamed repository"* | "")
	echo "*** Project description file hasn't been set" >&2
	exit 1
	;;
esac

# --- Check types
# if $newrev is 0000...0000, it's a commit to delete a ref.
zero=$(git hash-object --stdin </dev/null | tr '[0-9a-f]' '0')
if [ "$newrev" = "$zero" ]; then
	newrev_type=delete
else
	newrev_type=$(git cat-file -t $newrev)
fi

case "$refname","$newrev_type" in
	refs/tags/*,commit)
		# un-annotated tag
		short_refname=${refname##refs/tags/}
		if [ "$allowunannotated" != "true" ]; then
			echo "*** The un-annotated tag, $short_refname, is not allowed in this repository" >&2
			echo "*** Use 'git tag [ -a | -s ]' for tags you want to propagate." >&2
			exit 1
		fi
		;;
	refs/tags/*,delete)
		# delete tag
		if [ "$allowdeletetag" != "true" ]; then
			echo "*** Deleting a tag is not allowed in this repository" >&2
			exit 1
		fi
		;;
	refs/tags/*,tag)
		# annotated tag
		if [ "$allowmodifytag" != "true" ] && git rev-parse $refname > /dev/null 2>&1
		then
			echo "*** Tag '$refname' already exists." >&2
			echo "*** Modifying a tag is not allowed in this repository." >&2
			exit 1
		fi
		;;
	refs/heads/*,commit)
		# branch
		if [ "$oldrev" = "$zero" -a "$denycreatebranch" = "true" ]; then
			echo "*** Creating a branch is not allowed in this repository" >&2
			exit 1
		fi
		;;
	refs/heads/*,delete)
		# delete branch
		if [ "$allowdeletebranch" != "true" ]; then
			echo "*** Deleting a branch is not allowed in this repository" >&2
			exit 1
		fi
		;;
	refs/remotes/*,commit)
		# tracking branch
		;;
	refs/remotes/*,delete)
		# delete tracking branch
		if [ "$allowdeletebranch" != "true" ]; then
			echo "*** Deleting a tracking branch is not allowed in this repository" >&2
			exit 1
		fi
		;;
	*)
		# Anything else (is there anything else?)
		echo "*** Update hook: unknown type of update to ref $refname of type $newrev_type" >&2
		exit 1
		;;
esac

# --- Finished
exit 0

# Requirements

## Overview

Spec-Driven Steroids ships a CLI that injects a spec-driven workflow into AI coding tools. Two structural costs limit how far the product can grow.

The first cost is the runtime. The published package is a Node.js program with five runtime dependencies, so every user provisions a Node.js runtime and a package manager to install what is, functionally, a static bundle of prompts and a handful of filesystem commands.

The second cost is platform adaptation. Supporting a new AI coding tool currently requires writing code, not configuration: a scope resolver per platform, a format and frontmatter configuration per platform, and a transformation pipeline that rewrites canonical content differently for each target. Platform identity, content transformation, and injection orchestration are interleaved, which makes each new platform a change to runtime behavior rather than an addition to a registry.

This change re-architects the product around two commitments. First, the CLI becomes a first-class native Go binary with no runtime dependency, preserving the full command surface, exit codes, and output contracts that CI pipelines and users already depend on. Second, every SDS-managed artifact lives under a single platform-neutral artifact root — `.agents/` at project scope, `~/.agents/` at user scope — and platform differences are expressed as declarative descriptor data, so that adding a platform becomes a configuration change and canonical content is never rewritten per target.

The artifact root is not a new convention: the current release already writes MiniMax Code global skills to `~/.agents/skills`, Antigravity project scope to `.agents`, and Codex reads its native marketplace catalog from `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`. This change generalizes that location into the product's single artifact root. The root is a *shared* directory in some hosts, so the CLI owns only the paths it records and never removes content it did not create.

The change also consolidates the repository guidance artifacts: the contribution workflow and the code style conventions currently split across `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `STYLEGUIDE.md` become a single `CONVENTIONS.md`.

The distribution model changes with the runtime. GitHub Releases and Homebrew become the primary channels, while npm continues to serve as an installation channel that places the release binary for the user's platform. In parallel, the shipped artifacts gain a distribution form the AI tooling ecosystem already understands: a portable Agent Plugin package, plus the marketplace catalogs that let users install it from Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, MiniMax Code, and Gemini CLI without running the CLI at all.

Lane rationale: full. This change replaces the runtime of a published CLI, alters the on-disk layout that every existing installation depends on, rewrites the release path, and adds a publication surface to third-party marketplaces. Separate requirements, design, and tasks reviews resolve materially different uncertainties in the runtime migration, the artifact-root model, the packaging format, and the compatibility strategy.

## Glossary

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| Artifact root | The `.agents/` directory that holds every SDS-managed artifact, at project scope inside the repository or at user scope under the home directory. |
| Canonical artifact | A file whose content does not depend on the target platform and which SDS never rewrites to suit a platform. |
| Platform descriptor | Declarative metadata describing where a platform reads artifacts, how it names them, which frontmatter fields it requires, and how each artifact kind reaches it. |
| Platform-side artifact | A file written outside the artifact root because a platform reads its own directory instead of the artifact root. |
| Internal state | Install manifests and the template cache, which are SDS bookkeeping rather than injected artifacts and live in the platform configuration directory. |
| Portable Agent Plugin | A distribution package whose root holds a `plugin.json` manifest, a `skills/` directory, and an optional `mcp.json`, consumable as-is by several AI coding tools. |
| Marketplace catalog | The JSON document a platform reads to discover installable packages, listing each package name and where to fetch it. |
| Distribution channel | A mechanism that delivers the product to a user: GitHub Releases, Homebrew, the npm registry, or a platform marketplace. |
| Guidance set | The repository-level documents that the shipped guidance instructions direct the host to produce: `AGENTS.md`, `CONVENTIONS.md`, `TESTING.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, and `SECURITY.md`. |
| Legacy install | Files written into platform-specific directories by a CLI release published before this change, recorded in a version 1 install manifest or detectable by content match. |
| Rule graph | The local store of architectural decisions and workflow rules, held as JSON files with lifecycle state, provenance, and version history. |

- The Go toolchain and the release runners can cross-compile binaries for the supported operating system and architecture matrix.
- The remote template bundle and manifest schema stay backward compatible, so template bundles published before this change remain resolvable, and the required-skill contract remains the fourteen skill directories listed by the current registry.
- The version 1 install manifest format stays readable, so installations created by earlier releases can still be cleaned up and migrated.
- The npm package remains a public installation channel that places the release binary for the user's platform and architecture through platform-specific packages resolved by the registry.
- A Homebrew tap and a marketplace distribution repository exist outside this repository and are updated by the release pipeline.
- Marketplace vendors that require a vendor account, a submission form, or a human review keep that publication step manual.
- Marketplace listings that require open source are satisfied by the existing public repository.
- The landing page, the content of the individual workflow skills, and the hosting of the remote template bundle are outside the scope of this change.
- Users who already customized `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `STYLEGUIDE.md` keep access to their content during the consolidation into `CONVENTIONS.md`.

2.2 THE `sds` CLI SHALL use the same internal layout for skills, agents, and commands in the project artifact root and in the user artifact root.

2.3 THE `sds` CLI SHALL define the artifact root layout as a skills directory holding one directory per skill with its `SKILL.md` and references, an agents directory, and a commands directory, with the user artifact root additionally holding the stewardship subtree.

2.4 WHEN a project artifact and a user artifact share a name, THEN the `sds` CLI SHALL resolve the project artifact in preference to the user artifact, reporting the resolved artifact set with the layer that supplied each artifact.

2.5 THE `sds` CLI SHALL NOT create a platform-specific directory outside the artifact root unless the user selects that platform for injection, with the descriptor of that platform declaring whether the platform reads the artifact root directly or receives a platform-side artifact, and with the ownership of that directory recorded so that cleanup never removes it.

2.6 THE `sds` CLI SHALL report the resolved artifact root, the written artifact paths, and the effective scope in the machine-readable output of the inject command.

2.7 THE `sds` CLI SHALL own only the artifact paths it records in its install manifest, leaving every other content of the artifact root or of a platform directory untouched.

### REQ-3: Declarative Platform Descriptors Instead Of Code-Level Adaptation

**User Story:** As a maintainer, I want supporting a new AI coding tool to be a configuration change, so that the product can grow without growing a transformation pipeline.

#### Acceptance Criteria

3.1 THE `sds` CLI SHALL express each platform's artifact locations, per-operating-system and per-environment path variants, file naming, frontmatter composition rules, per-artifact-kind overrides, scope support, scope fallback, target-collision rules, legacy derivation rules, and post-injection actions as declarative descriptor data.

3.2 THE `sds` CLI SHALL emit the canonical artifact body unmodified for every platform whose descriptor declares the canonical format.

3.3 WHEN a platform descriptor declares a derived serialization, THEN the `sds` CLI SHALL derive the platform-side artifact from the canonical body using the transformation declared by that descriptor, with the descriptor stating the substitutions that serialization applies to the body.

3.4 WHEN a platform does not read the artifact root directly, THEN the `sds` CLI SHALL write a platform-side artifact containing the canonical body as the declared serialization transforms it, together with the frontmatter composed by the descriptor, without using symbolic links or pointer files for that purpose.

3.5 THE `sds` CLI SHALL record every written path and every platform-side path in the install manifest, with a content digest for each recorded file and with the producing platform recorded for each platform-side path.

3.6 WHEN a platform is added to the supported set, THEN the `sds` CLI SHALL require no change to the canonical artifact templates and no change to the injection orchestration code.

3.7 THE `sds` CLI SHALL reject a platform descriptor that omits the platform identifier, the display name, at least one supported scope, at least one artifact rule, or the required fields of that rule, reporting which field is missing.

3.8 THE `sds` CLI SHALL treat a requested scope that a platform does not support as the platform's declared fallback scope.

3.9 THE `sds` CLI SHALL resolve every path and state directory using the same environment variable precedence as the current release, including `APPDATA`, `USERPROFILE`, `LOCALAPPDATA`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, `SDS_CONFIG_DIR`, `SDS_TEMPLATE_CACHE_DIR`, and `SDS_HOME`.

### REQ-4: Compatibility With Existing Installations

**User Story:** As an existing user, I want my current installation recognized and migratable, so that moving to the rewritten CLI does not orphan files or discard my customizations.

#### Acceptance Criteria

4.1 WHEN the `sds` CLI looks for an install manifest, THEN the `sds` CLI SHALL read the manifest written by a previous release at the legacy filename key, which is `<platform>-global-global.json` for the user scope and `<platform>-project-<twelve hexadecimal characters of the pre-change platform root>` for the project scope, as well as at the current filename key, with the pre-change platform root of every supported platform declared as descriptor data.

4.2 WHEN the user requests cleanup of a legacy install, THEN the `sds` CLI SHALL remove a previously installed file only when its instruction body still matches the canonical body it was generated from, compared against the canonical body as it stood before this change and after applying the legacy per-platform derivation recorded for that platform, preserving and reporting every file whose body differs.

4.3 IF a legacy installed file was modified by the user, THEN the `sds` CLI SHALL preserve the modified file and report it instead of deleting or overwriting it.

4.4 WHEN the `sds` CLI injects into a project that contains artifacts written under a legacy platform directory other than the artifact root, THEN the `sds` CLI SHALL report as migration candidates those of those files that no current install manifest claims.

4.5 THE `sds` CLI SHALL read and write the version 1 install manifest format, including the recorded SHA-256 digest of each installed file, adding any new information as an additive field so that a manifest written by either implementation parses in the other.

4.6 THE `sds` CLI SHALL expose a dry-run mode for every command that writes to or removes files.

4.7 WHEN the `sds` CLI removes an empty parent directory after cleanup, THEN the `sds` CLI SHALL stop at the directory that owns the removed file, leaving that emptied owning directory in place and never removing a directory the install manifest does not claim.

4.8 THE `sds` CLI SHALL record the canonical artifacts of the artifact root separately from the platform-side artifacts of each platform, reconciling the claims of every manifest before removing a path so that removing one platform's installation never removes an artifact another platform still claims.

4.9 WHEN the backup option is used, THEN the `sds` CLI SHALL copy only the recorded artifact paths of the selected platform and scope without copying the whole artifact root.

### REQ-5: Consolidated Guidance Artifacts

**User Story:** As a user, I want one conventions document instead of separate contribution and style guides, so that my repository guidance is shorter to read and easier to maintain.

#### Acceptance Criteria

5.1 THE shipped guidance instructions SHALL direct the host to produce the guidance set consisting of `AGENTS.md`, `CONVENTIONS.md`, `TESTING.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, and `SECURITY.md`.

5.2 THE shipped guidance instructions SHALL direct the host to stop producing `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `STYLEGUIDE.md` as separate artifacts.

5.3 WHEN the guidance instructions are applied to a repository that holds `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `STYLEGUIDE.md`, THEN the host SHALL merge the existing contribution workflow and code style content into `CONVENTIONS.md` under section headings that preserve the original wording of user-authored rules.

5.4 WHEN the doctor command runs in a repository that holds `CONVENTIONS.md`, THEN the `sds` CLI SHALL report any `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `STYLEGUIDE.md` it also holds as superseded.

5.5 THE shipped guidance instructions SHALL direct the host to leave a guidance file that requires no change unwritten.

5.6 THE shipped guidance instructions SHALL direct the host to preserve user-authored rules when consolidating the contribution and style content, stating the merge rule that the guidance contract test asserts.

5.7 THE shipped guidance references SHALL discover `CONVENTIONS.md` in place of `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `STYLEGUIDE.md`.

5.8 WHEN this change ships, THEN the repository's own root guidance documents `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `STYLEGUIDE.md` SHALL be replaced by a single root `CONVENTIONS.md`.

### REQ-6: Behavioral Parity Of Validation And Stewardship

**User Story:** As a user, I want validators and stored rules to behave exactly as they do today, so that my CI gates and my accumulated knowledge keep working after the rewrite.

#### Acceptance Criteria

6.1 THE `sds` CLI SHALL produce the same validation verdict, error code, and diagnostic message for the same invalid input as the current release.

6.2 THE `sds` CLI SHALL classify EARS criteria, requirement identifiers, spec structure, and traceability exactly as the current release classifies them.

6.3 THE `sds` CLI SHALL read and write rule graph files in the existing on-disk format, so that rules stored before the rewrite remain retrievable.

6.4 WHEN the `sds` CLI stores a rule, THEN the `sds` CLI SHALL preserve the existing write lock and atomic-rename guarantees for the rule store.

6.5 THE `sds` CLI SHALL retain the exit code contract of the current release, where a successful validation exits with 0, a validation or partial failure exits with 1, and a usage error exits with 2.

6.6 THE `sds` CLI SHALL preserve the project-scoped rule resolution behavior in which a project rule takes precedence and retrieval falls back to global rules.

### REQ-7: Remote Template Bundle Continuity

**User Story:** As a user, I want the template bundles published before this change to keep working, so that the rewrite does not strand my installations.

#### Acceptance Criteria

7.1 THE `sds` CLI SHALL resolve a remote template bundle published with the current manifest and bundle schema, requiring the same fourteen skill directories that the current registry requires.

7.2 IF a remote bundle lacks a required skill contract, THEN the `sds` CLI SHALL fall back to the bundled templates and report the reason for the fallback.

7.3 WHEN the published manifest supplies a digest, THEN the `sds` CLI SHALL verify the bundle against that digest before use.

7.4 THE `sds` CLI SHALL reject a template bundle whose declared minimum CLI version is higher than the running binary version.

7.5 THE `sds` CLI SHALL embed the canonical artifacts in the binary, so that injection succeeds with no network access.

7.6 THE `sds` CLI SHALL preserve the containment, file-count, and size limits applied to a remote bundle before extraction.

### REQ-8: Release And Version Consistency

**User Story:** As a maintainer, I want one version source of truth, so that no channel disagrees about a release.

#### Acceptance Criteria

8.1 THE release process SHALL derive the binary version, the npm package version, the Homebrew formula reference, the template bundle version, and the marketplace package version from a single declared version in the repository.

8.2 WHEN a release is published, THEN the release pipeline SHALL publish the platform binaries, the npm packages, the Homebrew formula, the template bundle, and the marketplace package for the same version.

8.3 WHEN a release tag does not match the declared repository version, THEN the release pipeline SHALL fail before publishing any artifact.

8.4 THE release pipeline SHALL run the test suite and the packaged-artifact smoke check before publishing any artifact.

8.5 THE release pipeline SHALL publish the npm packages with the provenance attestation that the current release configuration requests.

8.6 THE release process SHALL update the Homebrew formula reference and the marketplace package version in the same release that publishes the binary.

### REQ-9: Portable Agent Plugin Packaging

**User Story:** As a user of an AI coding tool, I want to install the Spec-Driven workflow the way I install any other extension, so that I can adopt it without running the CLI at all.

#### Acceptance Criteria

9.1 THE `sds` CLI SHALL emit a portable Agent Plugin package whose root holds a `plugin.json` manifest, a `skills/` directory, and an optional `mcp.json`.

9.2 THE `sds` CLI SHALL generate the portable package from the canonical artifacts without altering the canonical artifact content.

9.3 WHEN the `sds` CLI emits a portable package, THEN the `sds` CLI SHALL reference every packaged skill in the `plugin.json` manifest.

9.4 WHEN a supported marketplace requires a vendor-specific manifest, THEN the `sds` CLI SHALL emit that manifest beside the portable manifest without altering the portable manifest, except for the Gemini CLI extension manifest, which belongs at the root of the distribution tree instead.

9.5 THE `sds` CLI SHALL validate the emitted package against the documented layout of every marketplace that consumes it, reporting each violation and rejecting an emitted tree that contains a symbolic link or a native binary.

9.6 THE `sds` CLI SHALL produce the portable package as a directory tree that a git repository can publish directly.

### REQ-10: Marketplace Catalogs And Publication

**User Story:** As a maintainer, I want one artifact set that the major tool marketplaces can consume, so that publishing to each of them is a push rather than a rebuild.

#### Acceptance Criteria

10.1 THE `sds` CLI SHALL emit the marketplace catalog, the root manifest, or the package subtree for every supported marketplace at the path that marketplace reads, reporting a registration step that is not a file as manual.

10.2 WHEN the `sds` CLI emits more than one marketplace catalog, THEN the `sds` CLI SHALL make every catalog reference the same canonical package directory and the same package version.

10.3 THE `sds` CLI SHALL emit each catalog so that a user can install the package from that marketplace without editing the catalog by hand.

10.4 THE `sds` CLI SHALL produce the package and catalog artifacts in a form that can be published by pushing them to a git repository, with the release pipeline generating that distribution tree outside this repository's working tree before pushing it to the distribution repository.

10.5 WHEN a marketplace requires a vendor account, a submission form, or a human review, THEN the `sds` CLI SHALL record that publication step as manual instead of attempting to automate it.

10.6 THE `sds` CLI SHALL report for each supported marketplace whether its publication step is automated or manual.

10.7 THE `sds` CLI SHALL keep the marketplace package version equal to the version declared for the release.

### REQ-11: Installer Trust Boundary

**User Story:** As a user installing from npm, I want the binary I receive to be verifiable, so that installing the CLI does not widen my trust surface.

#### Acceptance Criteria

11.1 THE npm installer SHALL obtain the binary only from the platform package that the registry resolved, never downloading it from another location.

11.2 THE npm installer SHALL verify the binary against the digest published with the platform package before placing it as a corruption check, refusing to place a binary whose digest does not match, while the publisher's attestation and the release-time checksum cross-check remain the provenance controls.

11.3 WHEN install scripts are disabled, THEN the published package documentation SHALL name the binary location inside the resolved platform package and the manual command that links it.

11.4 THE release pipeline SHALL cross-check the digest published with each platform package against the checksum published with the GitHub Release, publishing the platform packages before the main package that depends on them.

### REQ-12: Artifact Root Ownership

**User Story:** As a user who keeps my own agent skills in the shared agent directory, I want the CLI to touch only its own files, so that enabling it never removes or rewrites my work.

#### Acceptance Criteria

12.1 THE `sds` CLI SHALL remove only the artifact paths recorded in an install manifest, never removing a directory it did not create.

12.2 WHEN the artifact root contains an entry that no install manifest claims, THEN the `sds` CLI SHALL preserve that entry, including unrelated skill directories, treating such a directory as shared with other agents.

12.3 WHEN cleanup removes an empty parent directory, THEN the `sds` CLI SHALL stop at the directory that owns the removed file without continuing upward.

12.4 THE `sds` CLI SHALL report a legacy artifact as a migration candidate only when no current install manifest claims that path, never reporting a canonical artifact or a path claimed by a current manifest as a legacy candidate.
